deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of Part II of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857), from the section expressing log theta through integrals of algebraic functions. The next page is a letter dated 26 April 1857, which fits that dating. Notation: T is the Riemann surface of genus p. A point is eps=(s,z). u_1..u_p are the normalized first-kind integrals (period pi*i*delta on the a-cuts, a_{mu nu} on the b-cuts). alpha^(nu)=u(eps_nu) and u^(1)=u(eps_1), u^(2)=u(eps_2). The theta function is theta(v)=sum_m exp(sum a_{mu mu'} m_mu m_mu' + 2 sum m_mu v_mu). theta^(i) is short for theta(u^(i) - sum_nu alpha^(nu)).

(1) Object. Consider F = log theta(u^(2) - sum alpha^(nu)) - log theta(u^(1) - sum alpha^(nu)). It is viewed as a function of one point eps_mu, the others held fixed. The reading of the first argument as u^(2) is mine; it is the reading consistent with the stated singularities and with the final formula.

(2) Zeros. By the results of the preceding sections (previous page), theta(u^(i) - alpha(eps_mu) - sum_{nu!=mu} alpha^(nu)), as a function of eps_mu, vanishes at eps_i and at p-1 further points. Those p-1 points are determined by the eps_nu with nu != mu alone, independently of i. So their contributions cancel in F. As a function of eps_mu, F therefore has only two logarithmic singularities:
- like -log(z_mu - z_1) at eps_1;
- like +log(z_mu - z_2) at eps_2.

(3) Discontinuities. Make T simply connected by the cuts and the line from eps_1 to eps_2. From theta(v + a_nu) = exp(-2v_nu - a_{nu nu}) theta(v), F jumps by a constant across each line b_nu, namely 2(u_nu^(1) - u_nu^(2)) (up to orientation/sign convention). It jumps by 2*pi*i across the line from eps_1 to eps_2. Elsewhere it is continuous; in particular it is single-valued across the a-lines.

(4) Comparison function. Define varpi(eps_1,eps_2) as a function of eps with:
- the same logarithmic singularities;
- continuity everywhere outside the lines b and the eps_1-eps_2 line;
- a constant jump across each line.
This is the normalized integral of the third kind with vanishing a-periods. It is unique up to an additive constant. Write varpi^(mu) for its value at eps=eps_mu.

(5) Liouville step. F - varpi^(mu)(eps_1,eps_2) is a function of eps_mu without singularities or jumps, hence constant in eps_mu. The other varpi^(nu) do not involve eps_mu. So F - sum_{mu=1}^p varpi^(mu) is independent of all the eps_mu and depends only on eps_1 and eps_2.

(6) Normalization. Shifting varpi by C shifts the sum by pC. So one fixes the additive constant (a function of eps_1, eps_2) so that
 log theta^(2) - log theta^(1) = sum_{mu=1}^p varpi^(mu)(eps_1,eps_2).
This agrees with the previous page's Pi(eps_1,eps_2) = (1/p)(log theta(u^(1)-p u) - log theta(u^(2)-p u)), obtained by putting all eps_mu equal (up to sign convention).

(7) Global consequence. A finite change of any one of the pairs (eps,z),(eps_1,z_1),...,(eps_p,z_p) changes log theta by a sum of varpi's. Changing them one after another expresses log theta as a sum of third-kind integrals plus log theta(0,...,0), or plus its value at any chosen base configuration.

(8) The remaining quantity. log theta(0,...,0), as a function of the moduli, still has to be determined. Riemann says this needs considerations like those Jacobi used to find Theta(0). He records the heat equations:
 2 dtheta/da_{mu mu'} = d^2 theta/(dv_mu dv_mu') for mu != mu',
 4 dtheta/da_{mu mu} = d^2 theta/dv_mu^2.
Hence d log theta = sum (d log theta/da_{mu mu'}) da_{mu mu'}. These derivatives in the a's are expressible through algebraic functions and their integrals. Integrating leads to linear differential equations with algebraic coefficients (period / Picard-Fuchs type equations).

(9) Deferral. Carrying this out needs a further development of the theory of such functions, which he intends to give in a later paper.
errors: The display 'log theta^(2) - log theta^(1) = sum varpi^(mu)(eps, eps_2)' should read varpi^(mu)(eps_1, eps_2). This is a slip of the pen or of the transcription.

Sign conventions shift during the draft. The singularities (-log at eps_1, +log at eps_2) and the final formula (theta^(2) minus theta^(1)) require the first log theta in line 3 to have argument u^(2). The published version uses the opposite orientation. These are not mathematical errors.

The claim that changing a single eps_mu also yields a sum of varpi's ('in ähnlicher Art') is only asserted. It needs the symmetry argument (evenness of theta, interchange of the roles of eps and eps_mu); this is plausible but not written out.

The 'additive constant' fixed in step (6) depends on eps_1 and eps_2. That is legitimate, but it means varpi is fixed as a function of both endpoints only through this normalization. Riemann does not discuss its compatibility, e.g. varpi(eps_1,eps_2) + varpi(eps_2,eps_3) = varpi(eps_1,eps_3).

results.what: Difference of log theta at two points equals a sum of p normalized third-kind integrals: log theta(u^(2)-sum alpha) - log theta(u^(1)-sum alpha) = sum_mu varpi(eps_1,eps_2)(eps_mu)
results.modern_name: Expression of theta quotients / prime-form type identity via normalized abelian differentials of the third kind (Fay-type formula)

results.what: Uniqueness argument: a function without singularities and without jumps on the surface is constant
results.modern_name: Liouville / maximum principle on compact Riemann surfaces

results.what: Heat equations for the multivariable theta function: 2 dtheta/da_{mu mu'} = d2theta/dv_mu dv_mu', 4 dtheta/da_{mu mu} = d2theta/dv_mu^2
results.modern_name: Heat equation for Riemann theta functions
results.usually_credited_to: Fourier/Jacobi for genus 1; folklore for genus p (Riemann, Weierstrass)

results.what: Program: determine log theta(0) as a function of the moduli via Jacobi-type differential equations with algebraic coefficients
results.modern_name: Thomae-type formulas / Picard-Fuchs equations for theta constants
results.usually_credited_to: Thomae (1870) for hyperelliptic theta constants; Fuchs/Picard for period equations

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material that appears, essentially in this form, in Riemann's published 1857 paper: the expression of log theta by third-kind integrals and the deferral of log theta(0) to Jacobi-type considerations. The heat equation is standard. Only the explicit heat-equation programme for theta(0) is a mildly interesting unpublished detail.

checkable.asserts: 2 dtheta/da_{12} = d2theta/dv1 dv2, termwise for the genus-2 theta series
Index shift behind the quasi-periodicity theta(v+a)=exp(-2v-a)theta(v) (genus 1, Riemann normalization). It gives jumps of log theta differences equal to 2(u^(1)-u^(2)) across the b-lines.

checkable.sympy: C,p,S=symbols('C p S'); expand(sum([S/p+C for i in range(3)]).subs(p,3)-(S+3*C))==0
checkable.asserts: Shifting varpi by C shifts the sum of p values by pC (illustrated for p=3)

transcription_corrections: Line 3: the first term is log theta(u_1^(2) - sum alpha_1^(nu), ...), with something struck out before it, not log theta(u_1 - ...). This reading is required by the singularities stated (-log at eps_1, +log at eps_2) and by the final formula log theta^(2) - log theta^(1).
'(epsilon,z)' throughout should be '(s,z)' (varsigma, the algebraic function s), i.e. points eps=(s,z).
'in der Lage des Punktes' is likely 'eine Function, welche ... unstetig wird'; the phrase concerns the position (Lage) of the points eps_1, eps_2.
Final display: varpi^(mu)(eps_1, eps_2) rather than varpi^(mu)(eps, eps_2).
'abhängig von den Moduln' is plausible for the inserted phrase about log theta(0,...,0) as a function of the moduli.
Final line: 'die ich in einem späteren Aufsatze mitzutheilen gedenke' fits the image; the trailing 'wie' is uncertain.
